source_artifacts.locator: agent card for payments-agent (as consumed by the orchestrator)

capabilities.target: payments-agent task carrying the chosen vendor's bank details

inputs.source: Vendor quote emails and attachments from outside the company

instructions.note: 'Only pay vendors on the approved list' is the sole stated check on payment destination. It is a behavioral, model-dependent instruction, and it validates vendor identity only, not the bank account details carried in the same quote.

'Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks' assumes a downstream safety net. Runtime notes contradict this: payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task, with no further verification. This launders responsibility for a check that does not exist.
No bound on payment amount, frequency, or step count is stated, and max_unattended_steps / max_runtime_minutes are both unset, so the autonomy modifier applies to any S2/S3 sink this agent reaches.

controls.name: Manager approval of the purchase request (item and budget)
controls.decay_rationale: Human approval does not decay with model capability, but it is granted before any vendor quote exists, and the approval record is not passed to payments-agent (approval_context_propagates: false). It covers only in.purchase_request and provides no credit against cap.delegate_payment, where the actual vendor and bank details are chosen.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: only pay vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced only if the model chooses to check the vendor list before delegating payment. A more capable or more persistently injected model can rationalize an exception, and even when followed, the check validates vendor identity only, not the bank account details carried in the same untrusted quote.

controls.name: Bank-detail verification against a system of record, independent of inbound quote content
controls.decay_rationale: Not present in the design. If payments-agent compared the bank account to a previously confirmed value for the vendor and refused first-time or changed accounts without separate out-of-band verification, this would sever the vendor-quote-to-payment path regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Signed and pinned payments-agent card with mutual authentication
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. The card is fetched at startup, unsigned and unpinned, and the connection authenticates with a bearer token only (peer_identity_verified: false). Signature pinning plus mutual TLS or signed identity would close the impersonation / rug-pull path independent of model capability.

controls.name: Bind and propagate approval context (vendor and bank details) to payments-agent
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. Re-approving the specific vendor and bank details once a quote is selected, and passing a verifiable approval token to payments-agent that it checks before paying, would let payments-agent reject tasks lacking a matching approval, independent of what the orchestrator claims in the task payload.

controls.name: Human approval gate on payments-agent's pay_vendor action, raw action review
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. payments-agent currently pays automatically on receipt of a task from a trusted bearer token. A raw-action approval gate at the point of payment would be independent of orchestrator compromise or model capability.

findings.title: TC7/TC4: Approval granted before vendor selection, unbound context, and blind peer trust let an untrusted vendor quote direct an irreversible payment

attack_path.note: Manager approves item/budget before any vendor quote exists; approval record is not passed downstream.
Untrusted external email supplies the chosen vendor's quote and bank details; attacker-controlled content (classic business email compromise vector).
Orchestrator checks that the vendor is on the approved list, per prompt instruction, but this does not validate the bank account details carried in the same quote.

Orchestrator hands bank details from the untrusted quote to payments-agent via A2A; payments-agent pays based solely on the bearer token, with no verification against the original approval or against known-good banking details.

forecast.watch_signal: Model id/version changes in subject.model, orchestrator autonomy is increased, or task sessions grow longer, without adding destination (bank-detail) verification independent of the inbound quote.

evidence.observation: Orchestrator is instructed to collect quotes, choose the best one, and hand bank details to payments-agent with only a vendor-allowlist check; safety for the payment destination rests entirely on this instruction plus an unverified claim that payments-agent performs 'remaining checks.'

Manager approves the purchase request (item and budget) before any quote exists, and the approval record is not passed to payments-agent, so no approval covers the actual chosen vendor or bank details.

payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task, contradicting the prompt's claim that payments-agent 'will handle any remaining checks' — there is no destination verification anywhere in the chain.
Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company, so the bank details flowing into the payment task are untrusted (classic BEC vector).

recommendations.action: Verify payment destination (bank account) against a system-of-record banking profile for the approved vendor, independent of inbound quote email content, before payments-agent executes the transfer.
Bind the manager's approval to the specific vendor and bank details once a quote is selected, and propagate that approval record to payments-agent so it can verify authorization before paying.
Require a raw_action human approval gate on payments-agent's pay_vendor skill for payments above a low threshold, independent of the orchestrator's upstream approval.

findings.title: ASI04: Unsigned, unpinned payments-agent card enables impersonation or rug-pull of the payment skill

attack_path.note: Agent card is fetched at startup over A2A, authenticated with a bearer token only, and is not signed or pinned (definitions_pinned: false, peer_identity_verified: false).

If the card or endpoint is substituted (DNS spoofing, compromised internal host, or a rug pull between fetches), the orchestrator will delegate payment tasks, including vendor bank details, to whatever endpoint answers as payments-agent.

threat_refs.name: AI Supply Chain Compromise: AI Agent Tool

evidence.observation: Authentication scheme is bearer only; no signature or pinning fields are present.

The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned, so a substituted or tampered card (server impersonation, name collision, or rug pull between fetches) would be accepted without detection, and no control in the design covers this gap.

recommendations.action: Pin and verify the payments-agent card (hash pinning or a signed agent card) and require mutual TLS or signed identity for the A2A connection; reject unsigned or changed cards.
Replace the shared static bearer token with a per-call, scoped, short-lived credential tied to a verified identity rather than a token trusted blindly by payments-agent.

rating.rationale: Both findings start from a critical inherent tier: an untrusted source (vendor quote email, or an unauthenticated A2A peer channel) reaches an irreversible, delegated payment capability (cap.delegate_payment, S3 by reversibility and by action type), and the autonomy modifier applies because no step or runtime limit is declared. Finding 1's residual drops to high because the only control on the path, a prompt instruction to pay approved vendors, is behavioral and dependent, earning one tier of credit; the human manager-approval control exists but does not cover this path, since it is granted before the vendor quote exists and its context is not propagated to payments-agent (approval_context_propagates: false). Finding 2 has no controls at all covering it (the agent card is unsigned, unpinned, and authenticated only by a static bearer token payments-agent trusts unconditionally), so its residual stays critical. The rollup residual is therefore critical, driven by the unpinned peer identity gap, and the forecast stays critical because Finding 1's sole surviving control fails under a model upgrade or increased autonomy, returning it to its critical inherent tier as well. The single highest-leverage fix is adding a destination/bank-detail verification step at payments-agent that is independent of both the inbound quote content and the orchestrator's claims, combined with pinning and authenticating the payments-agent identity.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in prompt.md, the payments-agent agent card, and runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of either agent.

No MCP config, IaC, or source code was provided. The A2A credential scope and payments-agent's internal verification logic are inferred from the runtime notes rather than verified against code, so confidence on protocol-level findings is medium.
subject.model (provider/name/version) is not specified in the provided artifacts, so model-specific detail could not be recorded; the model_upgrade forecast trigger is still applicable generically.
autonomy.level (A3_act_then_report) was assigned by closest fit; no reporting or post-hoc review mechanism for the payment action is evidenced in the artifacts, which is itself a gap worth closing.
